body:
Gold is trading in rarefied territory today, and that context matters for reading the contract prices. Spot has been sitting in the $4,380–$4,400 range this month, with gold rising above $4,380 an ounce on Friday, recovering from earlier losses and securing a second consecutive weekly gain as investors assessed the Fed outlook. The rally has been driven largely by rate-cut bets and inflation data: prices opened at their highest level since early June following a disappointing employment report that prompted many analysts to pare back expectations of a Fed rate hike, with tensions in the Middle East also elevated after fresh strikes in the region adding a haven bid. That backdrop explains why both Kalshi's settlement strikes and Polymarket's touch strikes cluster so densely around $4,300–$4,700 — the market is pricing real uncertainty about whether this run continues toward the $4,700+ zone or stalls out.

The scanner flagged exactly one cross-platform pairing today, and it's a good illustration of why headline free money numbers are usually thinner than they look. Buying Polymarket's YES on gold touching $4,700 intraday in August (ask 7.9¢) alongside Kalshi's NO on gold settling above $4,731.99 on August 31 (ask 91¢) costs 98.9¢ for a $1 payout — but after fees the net edge is only about half a cent per contract, and the book only supports roughly $0.53 of total capturable profit. Part of the thinness is mechanical: Polymarket's contract pays out on any intraday touch of $4,700, while Kalshi's is a settle-price test at a different strike ($4,731.99) and a different moment (August 31, 5pm ET), so the two aren't quite the same bet — the tiny edge is largely compensation for that basis mismatch, not a clean arbitrage.

Otherwise it's a quiet day. Kalshi's year-end ladder (4,300 through 5,500) and its August 31 strikes are trading in an orderly, monotonically-declining pattern with no obvious mispricing, and Polymarket's weekly and monthly touch markets likewise look internally consistent. No unusual volume spikes or crossed books stood out.
headline: Gold's rally near $4,400 leaves only a thin, fee-eaten cross-platform edge
